newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU warns resentful Slovakia on democratic reforms.
newsitem.headline: EU warns resentful Slovakia on democratic reforms.

text.p: The European Union warned a resentful Slovakia on Tuesday it would closely scrutinise progress on democratic reforms when judging whether the former iron curtain country should be admitted to EU entry talks.

In a new sign that Brussels is dissatisfied with the pace of reforms on human rights and minorities, External Relations Commissioner Hans van den Broek said the lack of progress could also undermine economic reforms necessary to qualify.

"There's still some time before we will come forward with opinions...and it will contain our assessment of the situation at that time," he told a news conference after EU foreign ministers met Slovakian Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik.

"It's too early at the present time to draw final conclusions," he said, adding that the relatively low level of foreign investment there, affecting Slovakia's economic growth, reflected a lack of confidence in political reform.
"I think that that also has to do with the general conditions in the country and the confidence people have in political conditions," he said.
Hamzik said his country was committed to adopting the same democratic values as the EU and to doing what was necessary to be in the front rank of eastern countries to be admitted to EU entry talks.
"We are not the only ones who are undergoing a difficult and complicated process of reform...This is a process which is developing," he told the news conference.
Afterwards, suggesting that the EU should be more precise in its criticisms and stop generalising, he made clear he thought Slovakia was being picked out unfairly.
"I cannot agree with these general hesitations or judgments or doubts on the human rights situation or the situation on the national minorities," he told reporters.
"I think that the situation is very much comparable to the situation in the other candidate countries and also the countries of the EU."
The European Commission, the EU executive, is currently drawing up individual advice to EU governments on a list of 10 different applicant countries from central and eastern Europe.
The advice will be submitted shortly after the EU concludes the ongoing inter-governmental review of its workings, as it hopes to do in June.
The EU has said the former communist countries must make economic reforms and adopt the EU's same democratic values before they can open entry talks.

The EU has raised concerns about Slovakia's respect for democracy, law, human rights and freedom of expression. Legislation on the use of minority languages, which has still not been introduced, is a major source of concern to the EU.
The EU also urged Slovakia not to discriminate against its members when striking trade deals without countries like Russia and Croatia.
